sections.title: Everything from this unit, in one shopping trip
sections.content: A real shopping decision chains what you already know from this unit: numbers past ten, mennyibe kerül and -ért for price, olyan..., mint... for comparing, and választ plus biztos for the final call. döntés ("decision") names the whole thing, and nehéz ("difficult, heavy") is the adjective you'll want for a döntés that isn't easy — the same root behind nehezen ("with difficulty"), which you already know from A2 Unit 5.

items.spanish: Mennyibe kerül ez a szoknya? Háromezer forintba.
items.english: How much does this skirt cost? Three thousand forints.

items.spanish: Ez a szoknya olyan szép, mint a kék szoknya.
items.english: This skirt is as nice as the blue skirt.

items.spanish: Ezt választom háromezer forintért. Ez egy nehéz döntés, de biztos vagyok.
items.english: I'm choosing this one for three thousand forints. It's a hard decision, but I'm sure.

sections.content: You'll meet Meg making exactly this kind of decision in this unit's story — comparing, asking prices, and choosing confidently, all in the grammar you already have.
